project.summary: Synchronized multi-asset, multi-timeframe, cross-margin, limit-order, portfolio, and high-performance backtesting with local/Modal execution.
project.description:
## Outcome

Replace isolated per-asset batch semantics with a trustworthy Backtest Engine V2 that shortens time from strategy hypothesis to cost-valid evidence.

The first user-visible release is one strategy trading many assets through one shared Hyperliquid-style cross-margin perpetual account. The same foundation must support multi-timeframe data, conservative resting-limit simulation, post-hoc separate-account portfolio analytics, an opt-in fast strategy path, and remote Modal compute without later architectural replacement.

## Delivery policy

* Preserve V1 as the correctness oracle and fallback until each strategy proves parity.
* API and typed agent/research access precede substantial React UI work.
* Build one coherent set of contracts: synchronized market snapshots, target intents, portfolio allocation, venue/account snapshots, compact valuation series, and local/remote compute backends.
* Require causal closed-bar semantics, explicit data provenance, negative-path coverage, and reproducible saved results.
* First performance target: at least 10× V1 engine-compute speed on a warm-cache 96-asset × 50,000-bar summary fixture.
* Shared-account runs remain within one worker; scale independent runs and parameter variants horizontally.
* No live runtime, account, order, deployment, or capital mutation is authorized by this project.

## Explicit boundaries

* Hyperliquid cross-perpetual margin is in scope.
* Hyperliquid spot/borrow portfolio margin and isolated-margin mixtures are out of scope.
* Candle-level conservative resting-order fills are in scope.
* Historical L2 replay, queue-position claims, and latency simulation are out of scope.
* Funding belongs in the accounting contract but may be explicitly omitted when historical rates are unavailable.
* Live allocator adoption is a separately reviewed shadow/parity/canary gate requiring explicit capital authorization.

documents.title: Backtest Engine V2 — Architecture and Delivery Map
documents.content:
# Backtest Engine V2

## Decision

Build one coherent V2 architecture rather than independent patches. The first user-visible capability is one strategy trading many assets through one shared Hyperliquid-style cross-perpetual account.

V1 remains the correctness oracle and fallback. New strategies opt into the fast path only after parity.

## Core execution model

At each timestamp:

1. Update every market stream closing at T.
2. Mark all positions.
3. Freeze one pre-decision account snapshot.
4. Collect typed target intents from declared execution intervals.
5. Resolve the complete batch through proportional allocation with optional explicit priority.
6. Execute approved targets and account for costs.
7. Sample compact valuation state on the configured valuation interval.

This ordering must be invariant to asset iteration order.

## Key decisions

* Multi-timeframe data is native by default with an explicit derived option.
* Only fully closed bars are visible; incomplete higher-timeframe bars never leak.
* Binance taker-buy candle fields provide candle-level aggressor volume delta.
* Cross margin covers Hyperliquid-style perpetual positions sharing USDC collateral.
* Funding is represented in the accounting contract and explicitly omitted when unavailable.
* Post-hoc portfolios combine separate-account valuation series over their common overlap.
* Exact portfolio mode uses tested capital; what-if rescaling is visibly analytical.
* Resting limits activate after placement and require later-bar trade-through.
* Default fill capacity is 1% of opposite-aggressor base volume, shared by price-time priority.
* Historical L2, queue position, latency, isolated-margin mixtures, and Hyperliquid spot/borrow portfolio margin are excluded.
* Local V2 must prove at least 10× V1 engine-compute speed on the warm 96×50k fixture before Modal.
* Modal workers are research-only and receive no live credentials.
* Shared-account runs stay within one worker; independent runs/variants scale horizontally.
* Live use begins only with a non-controlling shadow comparison and a later explicit human authorization decision.

issue.title: Incorporate Databento US stock data into backtesting
issue.description:
## Outcome

Run trustworthy Money Machine backtests on a bounded US-stock universe using commercially licensed Databento historical data, with immutable source preservation and stock-specific correctness semantics.

## Why now

Stock research cannot currently reach a money test in the existing backtester. The research candle path supports Hyperliquid and Binance USD-M only; it has no stock provider, venue-neutral stock identity, corporate-action handling, or durable archive for purchased source files.

## Current-system attempt and observed blocker

The existing provider-qualified `backtest_candle` path and Binance/Hyperliquid loaders establish that research and live data can remain separate, but the provider dispatch and asset model are still crypto-specific. They cannot represent a stock across symbol changes, delisting, splits, dividends, and separate market sessions without adding semantics that do not exist today.

Related prior work: <issue id="6a1a75bf-54fc-457a-97c5-42606c2b3e61" href="https://linear.app/money-machine/issue/MON-113/backtest-historical-data-source-evaluate-binance-first">MON-113</issue> evaluated and implemented Binance as a deeper crypto historical source. Reuse that provider-qualified/cache pattern where it remains valid; do not reopen its Binance decision.

## Decision gate before implementation

Use Databento's metadata cost API and initial credit to price and acquire the smallest discriminating sample:

* Approximately 20 US securities covering liquid/illiquid names, ETF, recent IPO, delisted security, ticker change, split, and dividend cases.
* A bounded date range with regular and extended-hours observations.
* Start with unadjusted `OHLCV-1m`; include trades/BBO only for a few representative sessions where execution validation requires them.
* Confirm commercial/internal-use licensing and post-download retention rights before purchase.

Stop or narrow if the sample fails identity, coverage, corporate-action, bar-reconciliation, licensing, or projected-cost checks.

## Accepted scope

1. Select and document the exact Databento dataset, schemas, adjustment policy, session policy, and projected cost.
2. Preserve original Databento files as immutable raw inputs with request metadata, SHA-256 checksums, dataset/schema/version, retrieval time, and date boundaries.
3. Store one durable off-machine backup of the purchased raw files with versioning or object lock, and verify one restore. Keep local files as the working copy.
4. Introduce the minimum venue-neutral instrument identity needed for US stocks without silently treating ticker text as permanent identity.
5. Represent splits, dividends, symbol changes, mergers/delistings, and session boundaries explicitly. Do not overwrite raw prices with adjusted history.
6. Add a Databento historical loader behind the backtest-only provider boundary.
7. Normalize `OHLCV-1m` into the existing backtest candle contract and resample higher timeframes internally.
8. Make the bounded sample universe runnable through the normal backtest path and persist provider/source provenance with the run.
9. Reconcile representative outputs against Databento source data and test missing-bar, corporate-action, symbol-change, and session-boundary cases.

## No-build alternative

If there is not yet a bounded stock strategy question worth testing, retain the vendor/sample decision and defer ingestion. A CSV/manual one-off import is acceptable for a single exploratory experiment if it can preserve point-in-time identity and adjustment semantics. Do not build generalized stock-data infrastructure merely to expand platform coverage.

## Smallest implementation

One historical provider, one canonical input resolution, one bounded US-stock universe, local execution, and one durable raw-data backup. No generalized data lake, distributed ingestion service, live equities feed, broker integration, fundamentals, options, or full-depth order-book simulator.

## Work displaced

This is enabling work and should not displace active higher-confidence revenue experiments unless a specific stock hypothesis requires it. Do not expand the issue into cloud compute, generalized storage infrastructure, or live-equity execution.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Exact Databento dataset/schema/license and pre-purchase cost are recorded.
- [ ] The bounded sample passes documented identity, completeness, session, and corporate-action checks.
- [ ] Original source files, manifests, and checksums are retained locally and in one independently restorable off-machine copy.
- [ ] A restored raw object matches its original SHA-256 checksum.
- [ ] Stable stock identity survives at least one symbol-change fixture and does not rely solely on ticker text.
- [ ] Raw and adjusted/corporate-action semantics are explicit and tested.
- [ ] Selected stock symbols run through the normal backtest path from Databento `OHLCV-1m`.
- [ ] Higher timeframes are derived deterministically from the canonical minute data.
- [ ] Run metadata identifies provider, source dataset/schema, symbol identity, session policy, adjustment policy, and data boundaries.
- [ ] Focused tests cover missing minutes, split/dividend handling, ticker change/delisting, regular versus extended hours, duplicate ingestion, and checksum/manifest failure.
- [ ] No live runtime, account, order, position, deployment, or capital path changes are included.

## Follow-up gate

Only evaluate live stock data and brokerage providers after a stock strategy survives historical costs and has a justified paper/live test.

issue.title: Make recursive backtest indicators causal across rolling windows
issue.description:
## Problem

Backtest strategies receive a rolling candle window capped at 512 bars and recalculate recursive indicators from scratch on every candle. When the window advances, the indicator seed advances too. A historical value recalculated inside the new window can therefore differ from the value actually emitted for that timestamp.

Saved ETH 1d run `8703041c-1398-4edd-bb89-dc2d14d509fd` demonstrates the failure:

* 2023-10-26 emitted EMA 10/200 spread: `-0.215367`
* 2023-10-27 emitted spread: `+13.137372`
* 2023-10-26 recalculated inside the Oct 27 shifted window: `+0.142074`
* `emac_cross` compared positive → positive, emitted `0`, and missed the visible bullish cross.

This is a backtest-wide state ownership defect, not an `emac_cross`-only defect. Existing strategies already duplicate partial solutions: EMAC V4/V5 and PX threshold keep emitted-signal deques, while multi-speed EWMAC owns recursive EMA state.

## Outcome

Make recursive indicator values and crossing inputs causal and stable while retaining the bounded candle window. Future bars must not revise values previously emitted for decision use.

Historical-result compatibility does not matter. Do not preserve legacy behavior.

## Implementation plan

1. **Inventory affected strategies**
   * Find recursive indicators recalculated from bounded windows, beginning with EMA/EWMA users.
   * Find crossing and threshold decisions consuming recalculated `[-2]` values.
   * Separate finite-window indicators from recursive indicators.
2. **Add small shared state helpers**
   * Add a typed incremental EMA state helper initialized once and updated once per accepted candle.
   * Add a typed bounded emitted-value history helper returning canonical previous/current values.
   * Keep memory bounded and reset state with each strategy/run instance. Rely on the candle layer's existing sorted, deduplicated input contract.
   * Keep helpers strategy-owned; do not build a generalized indicator framework.
3. **Migrate affected strategies**
   * Replace recursive EMA recalculation used for decisions with the shared incremental helper.
   * Replace strategy-specific emitted-pair deques with the shared history helper.
   * Preserve signal mapping, thresholds, sizing, and execution semantics except behavior caused by revised historical values.
   * Remove dead duplicated state code.
4. **Verify causal behavior**
   * Add a real `BT_WINDOW_CAP=512` regression reproducing the October 2023 missed ETH cross.
   * Prove a value emitted at T is unchanged after T+1.
   * Prove incremental EMA equals one continuous causal pass within floating-point tolerance.
   * Test fresh-run reset, state isolation, and bounded memory. Do not duplicate candle-layer ordering/deduplication tests in strategy state.
   * Run focused strategy tests, Ruff, and typing checks.
5. **Run the corrected control**
   * Rerun the original ETH 1d EMAC-cross configuration with full retention.
   * Confirm the Oct 27 bullish cross is emitted and acted on.
   * Record the corrected run ID here and unblock <issue id="6729b02a-717c-430c-8222-849b948af120" href="https://linear.app/money-machine/issue/MON-210/complete-the-multi-asset-1d-emac-cross-control">MON-210</issue>.

## Acceptance criteria

* Recursive EMA/EWMA decision values update incrementally instead of being reseeded from shifted windows.
* Cross and threshold logic consumes consecutive canonical emitted values.
* Previously emitted decision values never change after future candles arrive.
* State is bounded, typed, and isolated by strategy/run. Ordering and deduplication remain owned by the validated candle layer.
* The October 2023 ETH regression emits the bullish cross.
* Applicable duplicated emitted-history deques use the shared helper.
* Focused tests, Ruff, and typing checks pass.
* A corrected full-retention ETH run ID is recorded and <issue id="6729b02a-717c-430c-8222-849b948af120" href="https://linear.app/money-machine/issue/MON-210/complete-the-multi-asset-1d-emac-cross-control">MON-210</issue> can resume.

## Out of scope

* Preserving or comparing historical backtest results.
* A legacy compatibility path.
* Live trading.
* A generalized indicator registry or engine rewrite.
* Strategy tuning or economic interpretation.
* Deployment or capital mutation.

## Related work

* <issue id="9d5c000e-8a40-4464-a1cd-e2d5945c4422" href="https://linear.app/money-machine/issue/MON-146/use-emitted-signal-history-for-emac-v4-threshold-crossings">MON-146</issue> fixed the same canonical emitted-history defect locally in EMAC V4.
* <issue id="42f15ea0-80a5-4db7-88be-2cc729b70ed3" href="https://linear.app/money-machine/issue/MON-189/build-lean-v2-featuredecision-kernel-and-migrate-emac-cross">MON-189</issue> is a separate performance/kernel project and is not required.
* This issue blocks <issue id="6729b02a-717c-430c-8222-849b948af120" href="https://linear.app/money-machine/issue/MON-210/complete-the-multi-asset-1d-emac-cross-control">MON-210</issue>.

issue.title: Review shadow evidence and decide whether to authorize a live allocator canary
issue.description:
## Human decision

Destin decides whether the shared allocator has enough shadow evidence to justify a separately scoped live canary.

## Required evidence

* Shadow observation period and population are explicitly stated.
* Current-live versus shadow differences are summarized by cause and severity.
* Order/sizing/margin discrepancies and counterexamples are included.
* Failure isolation, rollback, monitoring, and maximum capital/risk exposure are specified.
* Any unresolved strategy-priority or same-timestamp policy is presented as a decision, not inferred.

## Acceptance

* Decision is recorded as authorize bounded canary, continue shadowing, revise allocator, or reject.
* Authorization identifies exact account, strategy, assets, proof period, capital/risk limits, stop conditions, reviewer, and deployment path.
* If authorization is absent, no canary implementation or live control issue is created.

## Out of scope

This issue itself performs no deployment, order, account, strategy-lifecycle, or capital mutation.

issue.title: Audit current live decision scheduling against the V2 intent/allocator contract
issue.description:
## Decision

Determine the exact semantic gap between current asynchronous live strategy execution and timestamp-batched V2 allocation before any live adapter is built.

## Scope

* Trace live candle consumers, account snapshots, sizing, order paths, concurrent asset decisions, and failure/retry behavior.
* Identify where scheduler arrival order can affect capital allocation.
* Map live inputs/outputs onto `MarketSnapshot`, `TargetIntent`, and allocator contracts without changing runtime behavior.
* Define shadow comparison fields, acceptable differences, safety interlocks, and canary prerequisites.
* Search durable money-sensitive context and document unresolved capital decisions for Destin.

## Acceptance

* The audit names actual code paths and observed semantics rather than reconstructing intent.
* Every mismatch is classified as correctness, deliberate live behavior, nondeterminism, or unresolved product decision.
* Shadow mode cannot submit/cancel/alter orders or positions.

issue.title: Implement conservative trade-through limit fills with 1% aggressor-volume cap
issue.description:
## Outcome

Model useful candle-level passive fills while making no queue-position or depth claim.

## Scope

* Evaluate only orders active before the lower-timeframe bar.
* Buy requires later bar low strictly below limit; sell requires high strictly above limit.
* Fill at submitted limit price.
* Default participation cap is 1% of opposite-aggressor base volume, configurable per run.
* Resting buys consume taker-sell volume; resting sells consume taker-buy volume.
* Share one bar cap across eligible simulator orders using deterministic price-time priority.
* Apply configured maker fees and persist fill-model/version/provenance.

## Acceptance

* Touch without trade-through does not fill.
* Same-bar placement never fills.
* Partial fills and shared volume caps conserve available modeled volume.
* Better price then earlier time wins allocation.
* Cancel/replace and multiple-order cases are deterministic.
* Participation sensitivity can be run without code changes.
* Output is labeled candle-level conservative simulation, not L2 replay.

## Out of scope

Spread reconstruction, latency, market impact beyond participation, and exact queue position.

issue.description:
## Outcome

Resolve simultaneous multi-asset target requests against shared account/risk capacity without arbitrary loop-order capital consumption.

## Scope

* Accept one frozen account snapshot and a complete timestamp batch of target intents.
* Net intents by strategy/asset identity.
* Apply per-asset caps, gross/net exposure limits, initial-margin capacity, rounding, and minimum-notional rules.
* Scale equal-priority intents proportionally.
* Honor explicit priorities deterministically.
* Return approved, reduced, and rejected intents with reason codes.

## Acceptance

* Reordering input intents cannot change results.
* Two equal $8k requests against $10k capacity resolve to equal $5k approvals.
* Priority, ties, flips, reductions, close-only intents, and insufficient-margin cases are covered.
* Pure-function tests require no database, network, or live service.
* Allocation diagnostics are persisted-ready and strongly typed.

Live order submission or strategy-specific ranking logic.
